Youth-Led National Resilience Network

Cornerstones for Resilience

Today's Youth. Tomorrow's Resilience.

About

Cornerstones for Resilience - Youth is a youth-led national network connecting the dots of hazard mitigation, public education, house appraisal, insurance incentives, and resilience finance to improve disaster resilience.

To all youths: my future, I am in charge.

Vision

Laying cornerstones for community resilience by empowering today's youth to establish a systemic resilience mindset and conduct resilience education.

Mission

The vision will be fulfilled through establishing a national youth network to dance, sing, speak, convene and finance for resilience.

01

Age-Appropriate Education Programs

Develop and deliver age-appropriate hazard awareness and preparedness education programs and materials for K-12 students and the public, reviewed and approved by advisory boards composed of subject-matter experts and educators.

02

Youth Resilience & Public Speaking Training

Training youth nationwide in resilience knowledge and public speaking skills to effectively communicate disaster risk reduction and preparedness strategies, producing Resilience Ambassadors nationwide.

03

Resilience Education & Outreach

Nurturing the young generation for resilience by dancing and singing; increasing hazard risk awareness of the public and sharing hazard mitigation strategies using presentations.

04

Incentivizing Resilience via House Appraisal Change

Convening interagency forums to promote integrating resilience features into property appraisal, tailored to hazards such as tornadoes, hurricanes, floods, wildfires, and earthquakes — including researchers, policymakers, emergency managers, housing professionals, and community leaders.

05

Involving the Insurance Industry

Help researchers disseminate their most recent research to the insurance industry, expediting adoption of new secondary features related to resilience, leading to lower insurance premiums.

06

Resilience Finance (Resilience Bonds)

Money talks. Promoting innovative funding mechanisms such as resilience bonds to enable communities to take resilience actions prior to hazards — preventing hazards from becoming disasters.

Roadmap

Strategic Plan

Year 1

50 Resilience Ambassadors for one hazard (tornadoes) in Missouri, Oklahoma, Ohio, and Texas.

Year 2

50 Resilience Ambassadors for each hazard in multiple states across tornadoes, flooding, hurricanes, and wildfire — leading to 200 members.

Year 3

50 Resilience Ambassadors will be advanced to Resilience Fellows.

Year 4

100 Resilience Ambassadors for each hazard — leading to 400 members.

Accountability

Measurable Impact

  • Number of hazard-awareness education programs/materials developed
  • Number of resilience ambassadors trained
  • Number of presentations delivered by resilience ambassadors
  • Number of schools, summer camps, and communities reached
  • Number of interagency meetings convened
  • Number of travel awards
  • Amount of funds raised for disaster recoveries, travel funds, or cash awards

Summer Camp · Missouri S&T

23 New Resilience Heroes

← Back to News

Under the support of Professor Jami Swindell and Director Lindsey Elliott, Ms. Bobbie Stiritz of PCB Bank, Ms. Brandy Patrick of US Bank, and Mr. Scott of Rolla Fire Station, our first week-long summer camp was successfully held in the Interdisciplinary Building of Missouri S&T in the week of June 29, reaching 23 summer campers.

Campers role-played as citizens of five cities, each facing a different major hazard: St. Louis (tornadoes), Los Angeles (wildfires), Houston (flooding), Puerto Rico (hurricanes), and San Antonio (winter storms). To tell the “citizens” of each city apart, campers wore a color of shirt unique to their city, and took on roles such as mayors, emergency managers, and resilience officers.

Throughout the week, campers built their city, identified its leading hazards, and discussed their community’s priorities. They explored how to use economics and finance to move money in a positive direction — from reactive spending on disasters to proactive investment that prevents hazards from becoming disasters. Along the way, they learned how to make wallets to store their saved money, how to save in order to leverage sale opportunities, and much more.

Before the week wrapped up, campers sang their way through the different hazards and celebrated with an Independence Day dance party, leaving with a “Resilience Hero” Certificate.

Great thanks go to PCB Bank, US Bank, and the Rolla Fire Station for their strong support. Representatives from PCB Bank and US Bank joined as guest speakers, bringing real-world banking and financial decision-making to life for campers as they managed their own wallets and savings. The Rolla Fire Station shared a first responder’s perspective on hazard preparedness and community safety, giving campers a firsthand look at how their role-play towns connect to real emergency response in their own community.

Summer Camp · Kaleidoscope Discovery Center

21 New Resilience Heroes

← Back to News

Under the support of Director Martina Baur, Director Lauren, and Ms. Natalie, our second summer camp was successfully held at Kaleidoscope Discovery Center in Rolla, MO, on July 6–11, reaching out to 21 summer campers!

21 Resilience Heroes role-played as citizens of four hazard-prone cities, which are St. Louis (tornadoes), Los Angeles (wildfires), Houston (flooding), and Puerto Rico (hurricanes). They played such roles as Mayors, Emergency Managers, and Resilience Officers, … Together they built their cities, identified local hazards, and practiced moving money from reactive disaster spending to proactive prevention by leveraging economics and finance, while playing “Shark Tank” to develop hazards/disaster mitigation businesses to make money for their communities to thrive, achieving their resilience goals. The week wrapped up with campers singing their way through different hazards and celebrating the resilience goals they achieved.

Great thanks go to Ms. Bobbie Stiritz of PCB Bank and Ms. Brandy Patrick of US Bank for sharing real-world banking and financial decision-making with campers!

Why Join

Benefits of Members

  • Get training on public speaking for the topics of resilience.
  • Improve leadership skills.
  • Through monthly virtual meetings, listen and speak to distinguished speakers in hazards, disasters, insurance, business, economy and finance.
  • Establish systemic thinking for resilience.
  • Year-round, accumulate resilience knowledge from hazard experts through Zoom meetings.
  • Create opportunities for members to do TED talks.
  • Create opportunities for members to do podcasts.
  • Annual conference in various locations.
  • Members will be qualified to be evaluated to become Fellows after 2 years of commitment.
  • Get volunteer hours.
  • Get a shirt with the organization logo.
  • Get a chance to speak and practice leadership on various outreach events for this organization, such as in schools, summer camps, local libraries, churches, local museums, local science centers, local governments, community organizations, and public events.

RESILIENCE HEROES

Today’s Youth, Tomorrow’s Resilience

Build • Save • Protect • Innovate • Thrive

Imagine a society miniature where children build their own town, manage resources, launch businesses, leverage insurance, economics and finance to prevent natural hazards from becoming disasters (from Reactive to Proactive) and be prepared for unavoidable disasters (from Recovery to Building Back Better). This camp is offered voluntarily by Cornerstones for Resilience – Youth, which was developed by Cornerstones for Resilience – Youth and Missouri S&T faculty in Finance, Economics, and Civil Engineering. This camp teaches children business, finance and economics in the context of hazards, disaster and resilience. It introduces children to the skills they will need in a rapidly changing world: critical thinking, teamwork, leadership, financial decision-making, innovation, and resilience. It combines fun, creativity, and real-world learning in role-play, which is engaging and memorable. It is featured by experienced coaches and guest speakers from academia, banks and financial institutes, insurance institutes, and first responders of (e.g., fire chiefs), etc.

Becoming Resilience Heroes

Children today will face challenges that previous generations could not imagine. Extreme weather, technological change, economic uncertainty, and increasingly complex communities require young people to think systemically and creatively, adapt timely, and collaborate with others. Resilience is not simply bouncing back from adversity -- it is the ability to prepare, adapt, and thrive. This camp equips young people with the skills to become resilience heroes tomorrow.

What Makes This Camp Unique?

Most camps focus on one area, such as sports, coding, or arts. Resilience Heroes integrates financial literacy, entrepreneurship, engineering, leadership, and disaster preparedness into one immersive experience. Every activity connects to a big picture: building a thriving community and helping it succeed despite uncertainties. Campers gain resilience through role-play and hands-on experiences rather than lectures.

What Your Child Will Learn

💰Saving and budgeting
🤝Teamwork and communication
🧠Smart decision making
🚩Leadership and responsibility
🛡️Risk and insurance concepts
🏘️Community resilience and recovery
💡Entrepreneurship and innovation
🏔️Confidence in solving real-world problems

Please reach out to President Eva Liu for a deployment of this summer camp at your institute.
